ftp.infoText:
FTP root directory is the folder of the currently selected instance. Switching instances or saving new configuration will restart FTP automatically if it is running.
Devices on the same LAN can access via the IPv4 address above; external access requires port forwarding.
With IPv6 enabled, direct access is available via the stable IPv6 address (works within the same network; external access depends on carrier IPv6 public reachability, usually no port forwarding needed).

mcpPage.allowShellSubtitle: When on, AI can execute arbitrary shell commands on the device (run_shell/shell_cd)

mcpPage.enableSubtitleStopped: Enable to allow AI agent connections
mcpPage.infoText:
The MCP service runs within the app process using Streamable HTTP and stays available as long as the app is alive. AI clients on the same LAN connect using the address above, with 'Bearer <token>' in the Authorization header for authentication.
When 'Allow control operations' is on, AI can start/stop servers, send console commands and switch instances; when off, it can only read status, system resources, online players and logs.
Enable IPv6 to access via a stable IPv6 address directly (within the same network; external access depends on your ISP's IPv6 public reachability).
When saving new configs, the service restarts automatically if currently running to apply changes.

If UPnP reports a reserved IP (CGNAT), DDNS cannot make the server reachable either — use an FRP tunnel instead.
portMapping.enableStunSubtitle:
NAT hole punching lets players connect directly to your home broadband, with no relay server
Established when the server starts, closed when it stops
portMapping.stunHint:
The STUN tunnel probes a STUN server so your router keeps a public port reserved for this device; players connect straight to it. Speed is limited only by your upload bandwidth and no relay traffic is consumed.
Works only behind a full-cone NAT (NAT1): mobile data, campus networks and carrier-grade NAT (CGNAT) usually cannot establish a tunnel — use an FRP tunnel in those cases.

ssh.infoText:
Both SFTP root directory and SSH terminal initial directory are the folder of the currently selected instance. SFTP and SSH terminal share the same port, credentials, and host key, and can be toggled independently. Switching instances or saving new configuration will restart the service automatically if it is running.
SSH service requires username/password login and does not support anonymous access. "Allow Write" only affects SFTP; SSH terminal commands are not restricted by it. Please keep your credentials secure.
Devices on the same LAN can access via the address above; external access requires port forwarding. With IPv6 enabled, direct access is available via the stable IPv6 address.

mcp.tool.getServerStatus: Get the running status of the server process, current instance, and online players.
mcp.tool.getSystemInfo: Get device memory (MB), CPU usage, and server subprocess memory. -1 for cpuUsage means not yet sampled.
mcp.tool.getDeviceInfo: Get device hardware info: SoC, CPU architecture, manufacturer, model, Android version, and security patch.
mcp.tool.listInstances: List all server instances, marking which one is selected and which is running.
mcp.tool.getSelectedInstance: Get the detailed configuration of the currently selected instance (runtime, memory, Java version, server file, compat mode).
mcp.tool.getConsoleLog: Get the last few lines of the server console log (ANSI escapes removed).
mcp.tool.getConsoleLog.lines: Number of lines to return, default 100, range 1–1000.
mcp.tool.listOnlinePlayers: List currently online players (parsed from server log).
mcp.tool.startServer: Start the server for the currently selected instance. Auto-scans the instance directory for .jar/.phar, assembles startup arguments from instance config. Java Edition requires eula=true in eula.txt; returns an error if not set — agree to the EULA in-app first.
mcp.tool.stopServer: Gracefully stop the server (sends the stop command).
mcp.tool.forceStopServer: Force kill the server process (may lose data; use only when graceful stop fails).
mcp.tool.sendCommand: Send a console command to the running server. Examples: list, say <message>, op <player>, deop <player>, whitelist add <player>, ban <player>, kick <player>, time set day.
mcp.tool.sendCommand.command: The console command to send (without leading slash).
mcp.tool.selectInstance: Switch the currently selected instance (see list_instances for id). Does not affect a running server.
mcp.tool.runShell: Execute a shell command (<shell> -c) on the device, returning the exit code and merged stdout/stderr. Runs in the session's current working directory by default (see shell_cd/shell_pwd); can be overridden with the cwd parameter. Note: bare cd is not persistent across calls; use shell_cd or "cd x && ..." inside the command.
mcp.tool.runShell.cwd: Optional: working directory for this execution (absolute path).
mcp.tool.shellCd: Change the MCP shell session's current working directory (persistent, affects subsequent run_shell). Supports relative paths.
mcp.tool.shellCd.path: The target directory (absolute or relative to current).
mcp.tool.shellPwd: Return the MCP shell session's current working directory.
